class.name: TableCore
class.brief_description: Columns of fixed-width rows keyed by wire routes, and the store both the publisher and the receiver of those rows read back through.
class.description: A table is a view over routes, never a container of them. Any number of tables may key on the same route, which is what makes a component, a tag, and an edge all be tables rather than three mechanisms. Rows carry no identity of their own, so a row is exactly "what this table knows about that route right now". [codeblock] publish consume ─────────────────────────────── ───────────────────────────────────── write_routes(t, routes) read_routes(t) the applied row order write_column(t, i, data) read_column(t, i) the applied buffer commit(t, tick) snapshots read_births(t) / read_deaths(t) row_of(t, route) / rows_of(t, routes) [/codeblock] [method commit] is where atomicity is bought. Writes store the caller's arrays by reference, so a commit that did not copy could be torn by the next line of the caller's own loop. [method commit] validates every column against the row count and duplicates each buffer into the committed slot. After it returns the caller's arrays are theirs again, unconditionally. [br][br]Reads are the mirror image: they answer the store itself, which is what makes reading a 2,000-row column free. Treat a returned array as read-only and duplicate it to keep history, which is also the render-side interpolation pattern. [br][br]Births and deaths are derived here rather than decoded, so a dropped datagram can delay a row's data but can never lose a cohort. A birth is a route this table held no row for. A death is a row a removal took away. [br][br]A table declares nothing of its own. [method declare] binds a [SchemaRecord] that is already sealed, which is what makes the column order the wire order and [member SchemaRecord.shape_hash] the value every frame carries. [br][br][method apply_frame] absorbs ordinary datagram reordering rather than trusting arrival order. A frame older than the applied tick by more than a bounded window is skipped outright as stale, and inside that window a removed route is remembered a while after: an upsert for it that arrives late, having lost the race to its own removal, is dropped rather than resurrecting the row. [method begin_intake] opens a fresh wave, and every table [method apply_frame] touches accumulates its births and deaths across every frame of that wave rather than resetting between them, so a session reading [method read_births] and [method read_deaths] after several frames sees the wave's net cohort, not just the last frame's.

method.name: admit_header
method.description: Judges a frame header against this peer's own tables, the whole of the gate that does not depend on who sent it. [codeblock] Error ┠╴OK the frame addresses a table this peer agrees about ┠╴ERR_DOES_NOT_EXIST no local table carries that wire id ┖╴ERR_INVALID_DATA the header is truncated, the schema hash disagrees, or an unimplemented flag bit is set [/codeblock]

method.name: apply_frame
method.description: Applies one admitted frame to the receive store. [br][br]Returns the verdict beside the routes the caller must bind live, because this store holds no session and cannot reach the liveness core itself. [codeblock] Dictionary ┠╴verdict (Error) OK, ERR_SKIP for a stale frame, │ ERR_INVALID_DATA for a truncated one ┠╴table (RID) invalid on the lifecycle stream ┠╴tick (int) ┠╴bound (PackedInt64Array) routes this frame introduced ┖╴retired (PackedInt64Array) routes the lifecycle stream tombstoned [/codeblock]

method.name: begin_intake
method.description: Marks every table untouched so the next carrier intake starts a fresh wave.

method.name: clear_dirty
method.description: Clears [param table]'s dirty mark once its commit has reached the wire.

method.name: clear_session
method.description: Drops every table's row store, cohorts, and pending writes, keeping the declarations so a re-entered session finds the same tables under the same [RID]s.

method.name: column_count
method.description: Returns how many columns [param table] declares.

method.name: column_key
method.description: Returns one column's key, or an empty name when the address is invalid.

method.name: column_quantizer
method.description: Returns one column's quantizer, or [code]null[/code] for the memcpy path.

method.name: column_stride
method.description: Returns how many elements one row occupies in [param column], or [code]0[/code] when the address is invalid.

method.name: column_type
method.description: Returns one column's [enum SchemaCore.ColumnType], or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: commit
method.description: Snapshots the written routes and columns as [param table]'s applied state and marks it for the next tick boundary. [br][br]Every column must have been written and must be exactly [code]routes.size() * stride[/code] elements long, so a half table can never reach the wire. The snapshot severs the aliasing at the one edge where atomicity is bought, which is why the caller's arrays are theirs again the moment this returns.

method.name: count_bad_sender
method.description: Counts one frame refused because its sender was not the authority.

method.name: counters
method.description: Returns this core's drop counters under the lowercase [enum NetwMultiplayer.Stat] names the session merges its snapshot from.

method.name: declare
method.description: Binds [param table] to the sealed [param schema] whose columns its rows conform to. [codeblock] Error ┠╴OK bound, wire ids rebuilt ┠╴ERR_UNCONFIGURED the schema is missing or was never sealed ┠╴ERR_INVALID_DATA the schema declares a VARIANT column ┖╴ERR_ALREADY_EXISTS the handle is already bound to a different schema [/codeblock] A [constant SchemaCore.VARIANT] column is refused because variable width has no memcpy, no rows-per-frame budget, and no port. A value that shape leaves through [NetwChannel] keyed by the same route. [br][br]A schema with no columns is legal and meaningful: its table is a tag, and its commits carry membership alone.

method.name: dirty_tables
method.description: Returns every table holding an unsent commit, in declaration-stable wire order so two flushes in one session agree.

method.name: encode_frames
method.description: Encodes [param table]'s applied rows as self-contained upsert frames sized to [param budget] bytes each. [br][br]Every frame stands alone. There is no chunk index and no assembly, so losing one costs the rows it carried a tick of freshness and nothing else, where a commit needing reassembly would lose the whole tick. Pass [param snapshot] to mark the first frame [constant FLAG_SNAPSHOT], which tells a joining peer to clear the table before applying. [codeblock] payload ┠╴table id varint name-sorted wire id, 0 is the lifecycle stream ┠╴schema hash u16 0 on the lifecycle stream ┠╴tick varint the sender's commit tick ┠╴flags u8 SNAPSHOT | REMOVE | reserved ┠╴row count varint ┠╴routes varint per row ┖╴columns sealed order, each starting byte aligned [/codeblock]

method.name: encode_lifecycle
method.description: Encodes [param routes] as reliable route-lifecycle removals, the stream that tombstones an identity everywhere rather than in one table.

method.name: encode_removal
method.description: Encodes [param routes] as reliable removal frames for [param table]. [br][br]Membership subtraction rides the reliable lane because it must be exact and it is rare, so reliability costs nothing here.

method.name: is_reliable
method.description: Returns whether [param table]'s commits ride the reliable lane.

method.name: is_tombstoned
method.description: Returns whether [param route] has been retired here. [br][br]A row naming a retired route is dropped rather than resurrected, which is what makes a tombstone permanent without keeping the row it used to describe.

method.name: is_valid
method.description: Returns whether [param table] names a declared record.

method.name: lifecycle_removals
method.description: Returns the queued lifecycle removals without clearing them.

method.name: name_of
method.description: Returns [param table]'s declared name, or an empty name.

method.name: peek_header
method.description: Reads a frame's header without applying it, the material [method admit_header] judges on. [br][br]Returns an empty [Dictionary] when the header is truncated. [codeblock] Dictionary ┠╴table_id (int) ┠╴schema_hash (int) ┠╴tick (int) ┠╴flags (int) ┖╴rows (int) [/codeblock]

method.name: published_tables
method.description: Returns every table that has ever committed, the set a joining peer is owed a snapshot of.

method.name: queue_lifecycle_removals
method.description: Queues [param routes] for the reliable route-lifecycle stream, which is what the authority owes every peer once it has released an identity.

method.name: read_births
method.description: Returns the routes the most recent applied wave added.

method.name: read_column
method.description: Returns one applied column. Treat it as read-only and duplicate it to keep history.

method.name: read_deaths
method.description: Returns the routes the most recent applied wave removed.

method.name: read_routes
method.description: Returns the applied row order. Treat it as read-only.

method.name: retire_routes
method.description: Retires [param routes] here: they become tombstones and their rows leave every table that held one. [br][br]The authority runs this the moment it releases an identity and every other peer runs it when the lifecycle frame lands, so the host and a client end up in the same state through the same code. Pass [param as_wave] on the receive path, where the removal belongs to the intake's cohorts rather than to a commit's.

method.name: row_of
method.description: Returns [param route]'s row index, or [code]-1[/code] when it has no row.

method.name: rows_of
method.description: Returns one row index per entry of [param routes], [code]-1[/code] where the route has no row. [br][br]The join primitive. One crossing answers a whole join, where a per-row [method row_of] loop would be a per-row crossing in everything but name.

method.name: schema_hash
method.description: Returns [param table]'s sealed schema hash, or [code]0[/code] when it is not sealed. The hash rides every frame, so mid-session script reload skew is caught rather than only join-time skew.

method.name: set_reliable
method.description: Sets whether commits ride the reliable lane. [br][br]Local configuration rather than shape, so it never enters [method schema_hash] and may be written at any time.

method.name: table_from_wire_id
method.description: Returns the table [param id] addresses, or an invalid [RID].

method.name: take_lifecycle_removals
method.description: Returns the queued lifecycle removals and clears the queue, so one flush emits each retired route exactly once.

method.name: take_pending_removals
method.description: Returns the routes peers still hold rows for that [param table] no longer has, and adopts the current row set as what they will hold once this flush leaves. [br][br]Membership subtraction is measured against what was last sent rather than against the previous commit, because several commits inside one tick collapse to the last and only the difference from the wire is owed.

method.name: tick_of
method.description: Returns the tick of the freshest applied row set, or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: touched_tables
method.description: Returns every table an intake applied a frame to, the set [signal NetwMultiplayer.table_received] is emitted once per.

method.name: wire_bits
method.description: Returns how many bits one element of [param type] occupies unquantized, which is what [method encode_frames] plans its row budget against. [br][br][constant SchemaCore.ENTITY] is a varint, counted at its worst case. [constant SchemaCore.VARIANT] answers [code]0[/code], because variable width is unplannable and a table refuses it at [method declare].

method.name: wire_id
method.description: Returns [param table]'s wire id, the name-sorted position among sealed tables counted from [code]1[/code], or [code]0[/code] when it is not sealed. [br][br]Sorted as [String] rather than [StringName], because [StringName] ordering is by internal pointer and two peers would disagree about it. The whole point of a name-sorted id is that both ends compute the same one without negotiating. [br][br]Id [code]0[/code] is never a table. It names [constant LIFECYCLE_STREAM].

method.name: write_column
method.description: Records one column's buffer for the next [method commit]. [br][br]The buffer is held by reference and copied at [method commit], so writing is a slot store rather than a copy. [param data] must be the storage array [method SchemaCore.storage_type] names for that column's type. A [constant SchemaCore.QUATERNION] column stores as a [PackedVector4Array]; its [method column_quantizer], if any, still reads and writes actual [Quaternion] values, converted at the boundary.

method.name: write_routes
method.description: Records the row order the next [method commit] will publish.

constants.constant: Frame flag: the receiver clears the table, then applies this frame's rows. The first frame of a late-join heal carries it and the rest are plain upserts on the same ordered reliable lane, which is what makes a chunked snapshot coherent without an assembly protocol.
Frame flag: the payload is routes only and those rows are removed. On the lifecycle stream it additionally tombstones them everywhere.
Frame flag, reserved: row identity is a (source, target) pair.
Frame flag, reserved: rows have no identity, an event stream.

The flag bits this implementation reads. A frame carrying any other bit is refused whole by [method admit_header], because a receiver that cannot name a bit cannot know what the rest of the payload means.
The wire id that names the route lifecycle stream rather than a table.
Bytes reserved for one frame's own header and the envelope that carries it, subtracted from the carrier budget before rows are planned.
